ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Mary McLeod Bethune

text.paragraph: Subsequent annual wellness visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mrs. Bethune, now 73, returns for her subsequent annual wellness visit, eight weeks after her asthma review. She has had no night waking and uses the reliever inhalation about once a week; her peak flow stays between 320 and 345 L/min. She travelled to Washington twice more for the council's meetings without trouble. She walks on the campus most mornings and has seen the dietitian. Home blood pressure averages 124/74. She completed the health risk assessment beforehand and asked to put her wishes about her care in writing. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-09-21; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well and upright; weight 86.0 kg, BMI 32.4; blood pressure 126/76, pulse 70
Whispered-voice test passed on both sides
Regular rhythm; no murmur; no edema
Timed Up and Go 11 seconds; rises from a chair without using her arms

Wheeze, cough and breathlessness for four months: waking with cough and tight chest two or three nights a week, breathless on one flight of stairs, relieved by albuterol, worse with colds, dust and strong scents; known asthma for many years but never confirmed by lung function testing and never treated with an inhaled steroid. Asthma, COPD and heart failure to be distinguished: spirometry with bronchodilator response, FeNO and an echocardiogram booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented chronic asthma. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Blocked nose, thick postnasal drip and a reduced sense of smell for years, worse in the last year; no nosebleeds; never seen by an ear, nose and throat specialist
S — Synthetic upper-airway symptoms; superseded by the diagnosis of chronic rhinosinusitis after nasal endoscopy.
Gastro-esophageal reflux: heartburn and an acid taste two or three evenings a week, worse after late meals and lying down; no trouble swallowing, vomiting, black stools or weight loss
S — Synthetic comorbidity of asthma; not a claim about her real health.
Obesity, class 1 (BMI 33.1); she wants to walk more and to keep up with her work, and agreed to talk about it
S — Synthetic comorbidity recorded in her words and with her agreement; not a claim about her real weight.

Moderate asthma exacerbation triggered by a cold: two days of worsening wheeze and night waking despite eight reliever inhalations a day, peak flow 205 L/min (60 percent of her best), oxygen saturation 94 percent; improved to 275 L/min in clinic; treated without admission; resolved
S — Synthetic exacerbation; not a claim about a real attack.

Asthma, confirmed: variable airflow obstruction (FEV1 64 percent predicted, rising 270 mL or 21 percent after bronchodilator, with a normal post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC of 0.72 and normal DLCO); type 2 inflammation (FeNO 46 ppb, blood eosinophils 0.42 x10^3/uL, total IgE 210, house dust mite sensitization); not COPD and not heart failure. Uncontrolled at diagnosis on albuterol alone
S — Synthetic modern confirmation linked to her documented chronic asthma.

Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure: clinic blood pressure 152/88 and 146/86, home average 144/84; mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with grade 1 diastolic dysfunction and a normal ejection fraction (62 percent); BNP 48 pg/mL
S — Synthetic finding of the modern work-up; not a claim about her real heart.
Hyperlipidemia: LDL cholesterol 144 mg/dL; 10-year ASCVD risk above 20 percent with hypertension
Chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps: years of congestion, postnasal drip and reduced smell, with mucosal swelling and mucus in both middle meatuses and no polyps on nasal endoscopy
S — Synthetic upper-airway comorbidity of asthma; not a claim about her real health.

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 25 minutes, with her consent. She named a health care surrogate, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here, and completed a Florida designation of health care surrogate and a living will. She wants full treatment for an asthma attack or any illness she could recover from, including a breathing machine for a short time if needed. If she had an illness from which she could not recover and could no longer recognize people or speak for herself, she would not want resuscitation or a breathing machine, and would want comfort care at home, with her family, her colleagues and her church. To be revisited at any change in her health and at least yearly. [S]
